cap_note: Deliberate cap of ≤4 test cases per explicit user instruction, overriding this skill's default one-per-FR breadth. Cases are selected for highest-value coverage, not enumerated per FR; FR-1/FR-3 are intentionally left uncovered at this level — see coverage_audit.uncovered. FIX-02 (2026-09-03) added SHP-01-TC-05 and SHP-01-TC-06 above the original <=4 cap: they close coverage gaps on already-merged code (FR-3, and getProgramStyle's fallback/reference behaviour) rather than widening story scope. FR-1 remains deliberately uncovered.

test_cases.title: formatPersonaTag resolves all four persona tag/subtitle literals; cio and any invalid value throw
test_cases.given: the persona-context header renders for a resolved persona value
test_cases.when: the shell computes the persona tag and subtitle for each of the four valid personas, and for `cio`/any invalid value
test_cases.then: each valid persona renders its exact tag and subtitle literal; `cio` or any other invalid value throws rather than rendering a fabricated or blank tag
test_cases.objective: Verify formatPersonaTag()/the persona-context header render the correct tag + subtitle literal for each of the 4 valid personas, and throw for `cio` or any unrecognized persona value instead of falling back to a fabricated or blank tag.
preconditions: Test harness can render the persona-context header (or call formatPersonaTag() directly) with session and program already resolved — the loading gate has already passed
steps: Render/evaluate with persona='architect' and assert tag/subtitle text
Repeat for persona='developer'
Repeat for persona='product-manager'
Repeat for persona='engineering-manager'
Render/evaluate with persona='cio' and capture the thrown error
Render/evaluate with an arbitrary invalid string and capture the thrown error
expected_results: architect renders tag 'Architect' and subtitle 'Architect overview'
developer renders tag 'Developer' and subtitle 'Developer overview'
product-manager renders tag 'Product Manager' and subtitle 'Product Manager overview'
engineering-manager renders tag 'Eng Manager' and subtitle 'Engineering manager overview' — the lowercase 'm' verified byte-exact
cio throws; no tag, no fabricated string, no blank render
an arbitrary invalid persona string throws the same way

test_cases.title: Shell suppresses all persona-gated regions while loading, shows the neutral error state on resolver raise or cio, and the identity bar falls back to neutral when signedInUser is undefined
test_cases.given: session and/or persona-resolver output have not yet resolved, or the persona-resolver raises (or a `cio` value reaches the shell), or `signedInUser` is undefined
test_cases.when: the shell is asked to render
test_cases.then: while pending, only the static product header renders (identity bar, persona tag, subtitle, program context all suppressed, no skeleton); on raise/cio, a neutral gray 'Persona unavailable' badge replaces the persona tag, no subtitle renders, and a visually-hidden aria-live='assertive' region announces 'Unable to load your dashboard view.'; when `signedInUser` is undefined the identity bar shows its neutral fallback, never a placeholder name
test_cases.objective: Verify the loading state suppresses every persona-gated region with no partial/mismatched render, the error state shows the exact neutral badge/copy/aria-live announcement on a resolver raise or cio, and the identity bar degrades to a neutral fallback (never a placeholder name) when signedInUser is undefined — the single data-presence mechanism the phased, no-feature-flag rollout depends on.
preconditions: Test harness can render PersonaDashboardShell with session/persona/signedInUser controlled independently
A PersonaNotFoundError-raising persona-resolver stub is available
steps: Render the shell with session and persona both unresolved (null)
Assert only the static product header is present; identity bar, persona tag, subtitle, program context are all absent — no skeleton markup
Render the shell with the persona-resolver stub throwing PersonaNotFoundError

Assert a neutral gray badge reading exactly 'Persona unavailable' replaces the persona tag, no subtitle renders, and a visually-hidden element with aria-live='assertive' contains 'Unable to load your dashboard view.'
Render the shell with persona='cio' reaching the component directly
Assert the same neutral badge/announcement as the raise case
Render the shell with signedInUser=undefined while session/persona are otherwise resolved
Assert the identity bar renders its neutral fallback, with no placeholder name/jobTitle text
expected_results: Loading: no persona-gated region rendered, only the static header, no skeleton
Raise: badge text is exactly 'Persona unavailable'; subtitle absent; aria-live='assertive' region present with exact copy 'Unable to load your dashboard view.'
cio: identical neutral badge/announcement as the raise case — the fail-loud path never reaches render with a fabricated tag
signedInUser undefined: identity bar shows the neutral fallback, no placeholder name/jobTitle rendered

test_cases.title: Program-context block passes icon/name/type/description through unchanged and composes avatarStyle/type-chip color itself, ignoring any caller-supplied style field
test_cases.given: a program object (icon, name, type, description) is supplied by the composing dashboard page
test_cases.when: the persona-shell renders the program-context block
test_cases.then: icon, name, type tag text, and description render unchanged from the prop, and the type-chip color / avatar style are computed by the shell from its own docs/design/tokens.md lookup keyed on program.type — never from a style value on the prop, even if one is present
test_cases.objective: Verify the program-context block passes icon/name/type/description through verbatim and independently derives avatarStyle/type-chip color from a program.type lookup table, confirming the shell never reads or applies caller-supplied CSS.
preconditions: Test harness renders the program-context block with session+persona already resolved
The docs/design/tokens.md type-chip color lookup table is available to the test for cross-check

program_a.name: Payments & Billing
program_a.description: Migration from monolithic core to event-driven microservices, with PCI-compliant tokenization

steps: Render the program-context block with program_a
Assert icon, name, description render verbatim and the type chip reads 'Migration'
Cross-check the rendered type-chip color/avatarStyle against the tokens.md lookup for type='Migration' (#2a6fdb on #eaf1fc), accounting for jsdom's rgb() normalisation
Render the program-context block with program_b_with_injected_css, which carries an extraneous avatarStyle field
Assert icon/name/description still render verbatim and the type chip reads 'Maintenance'

Assert the rendered avatarStyle/type-chip color matches the tokens.md lookup for type='Maintenance' (#c08a1e on #fdf3e0), NOT the injected 'background:#ff0000' value, and that #ff0000/rgb(255, 0, 0) appears nowhere in the output
expected_results: program_a: icon/name/description unchanged, type chip 'Migration', style matches tokens.md lookup for 'Migration'
program_b: icon/name/description unchanged, type chip 'Maintenance', style matches tokens.md lookup for 'Maintenance' — the injected avatarStyle field is never applied
test_cases.test_data_note: Reconciled 2026-09-03 (FLAGS.md AF-06, verdict accept). The original test_data keyed on type='infrastructure'/'product', neither of which exists in docs/design/tokens.md § Program type colors (Migration / Greenfield feature development / Brownfield feature development / Maintenance, byte-exact from the EMD mockup's tMap). Those steps were unsatisfiable as written — 'infrastructure' resolves to the Migration fallback, so the cross-check would have passed vacuously. tasks.json T-09 already directed the substitution to real types; this reconciles the manifest to what the test asserts.

test_cases.title: Shell render completes within the 200ms p95 budget once session and persona-resolver output are available
test_cases.given: session and persona-resolver output are already available as resolved props
test_cases.then: render completes within 200ms p95, since the shell performs no I/O of its own and the budget covers render time only
test_cases.objective: Verify the presentational shell's render time from already-resolved props stays within the 200ms p95 budget, isolating render cost from the upstream fetch/resolve time owned by the composing pages.
preconditions: session, persona, and program props are pre-resolved — no async fetch inside the timed window
Benchmark harness (vitest bench or performance.now() around render) runs ≥30 iterations for a stable p95
steps: Mount PersonaDashboardShell with fully-resolved session/persona/program props
Measure render duration via performance.now() around the render call, repeated for 30 iterations
Compute p95 render duration across iterations

test_cases.title: deriveInitials derives initials from a display name, including the single-token case
test_cases.given: a signed-in user's display name is available as a plain string
test_cases.when: the shell derives the initials rendered inside the identity avatar
test_cases.then: the first letter of each of the first two whitespace-separated tokens is uppercased; a single-token name yields that one letter only, never doubled
test_cases.objective: Close the FR-3 coverage gap. deriveInitials is a pure string function with no dependency on the AUTH-01 session-contract amendment, so the original deferral reasoning did not apply to it.
steps: Assert each of the four mockup identity names yields its initials
Assert a >2-token name uses only the first two tokens
Assert lower-case input is uppercased
Assert whitespace runs do not emit empty initials
Assert a single-token name yields one letter, not a doubled pair
Assert empty/whitespace-only input returns an empty string (documents current behaviour; unspecified)
expected_results: All four mockup names match their identity-bar initials
Single-token name yields exactly one letter (logged assumption, docs/stories/SHP-01.md § Decision log)
No empty or doubled initials for any whitespace shape

test_cases.title: getProgramStyle falls back to Migration for an unknown type and returns independent style objects
test_cases.given: a program.type value supplied by the composing page
test_cases.when: the shell resolves the avatar/type-chip colour pair for it
test_cases.then: a known type yields its docs/design/tokens.md pair; an unrecognised type falls back to Migration rather than throwing; avatarStyle and typeChip are independent objects
test_cases.objective: Close the direct-coverage gap on getProgramStyle. TC-03 exercised it only indirectly through a rendered component and never covered the unknown-type fallback (condition C-3's fail-soft contrast with formatPersonaTag's fail-loud) or REVIEW.md F-3's shared object reference.
steps: Assert each of the 4 tokens.md types maps to its exact colour pair
Assert each unrecognised type resolves to Migration's pair without throwing
Assert avatarStyle and typeChip are equal in value but not the same object
Assert mutating one call's result does not affect another call
expected_results: All 4 known types match tokens.md § Program type colors
Unknown types fall back to Migration, never throw (contrast with formatPersonaTag)
avatarStyle !== typeChip by reference (REVIEW.md F-3 closed)

acceptance_criteria.note: Product header text + persona tag portion covered by TC-01; the identity bar's absent-signedInUser neutral-fallback path covered by TC-02. The populated-identity render (real name/jobTitle values) is NOT separately asserted at this cap — see uncovered SHP-01-FR-1.

TC-02 exercises the one stable, testable slice — the `undefined` path — without asserting populated field names.

Covered as of 2026-09-03 by FIX-02: apps/web/src/lib/deriveInitials.test.ts. The original deferral reasoned that initials derivation 'depends on the same unlanded signedInUser.name shape as FR-1', but deriveInitials(name: string) takes a plain string and is unaffected by the prop shape or field name — so it was testable all along. FR-1 remains genuinely deferred.

The aria-live='assertive' announcement is asserted inside TC-02. The ≥4.5:1 contrast-ratio check on the four persona tag/background color pairs is explicitly routed to design QA in DESIGN.md per the PRD, not this manifest.
